final_answer: All eight decision atoms cleared the judge with high scores (totals 0.955–1.0) and there were no conflicts or micro-debates to resolve, so the final record ACCEPTS all eight and rejects none. The agreed plan upgrades the OKO recognition pipeline to YOLOv11x (the maximum model), optimizes the confidence threshold quantitatively rather than by eye, and proves the change with a fair, reproducible before/after comparison: the same recorded clip from real camera device 0 is run through both the baseline and yolo11x, accuracy metrics (mAP/precision/recall/F1) are computed on labeled data (a small hand-labeled device-0 proof-set and/or COCO val), and a separate live run on device 0 confirms error-free real-time processing. Performance cost (FPS/latency) is measured and reported explicitly — including an honest statement of whether yolo11x can sustain real-time on the actual hardware — and every artifact (raw clip, annotated before/after frames, metrics JSON/CSV, config snapshots, final report) is persisted as proof. The single largest residual risk is the absence of true ground-truth labels for device-0 footage and uncertain GPU availability, both captured as open questions to settle before claiming accuracy gains.

decisions.decision: Adopt YOLOv11x as the target model, set explicitly in config and verified at load time.
decisions.rationale: Directly satisfies the core contract constraint ('use yolo11x as the maximum model'). Cheap, fully reversible, and verification-by-log eliminates the most common failure mode — silently running the old weights while believing the upgrade happened.
alternatives_considered: Keep current baseline weights
Use a lighter tier (yolo11l/m) for speed
Pass the model as a runtime CLI arg instead of pinning it in config
decisions.risk: yolo11x.pt download (~110MB) or version mismatch in ultralytics could fail silently; mitigated by the load-time assertion.
decisions.test: Verify `model_file` in config points to `yolo11x.pt` and startup logs confirm `yolo11x` was loaded (param count / model summary).

decisions.decision: Run the before/after comparison on the SAME recorded clip captured from real camera device 0.
decisions.rationale: A frozen input is the only way to make baseline vs yolo11x differences attributable to the model rather than to scene variation. Reproducible and re-runnable on demand.
alternatives_considered: Benchmark each model against its own separate live stream (non-comparable)
Use only stock COCO images (not from device 0, fails the 'real camera' constraint)
decisions.risk: A single short clip may not exercise the conditions where yolo11x helps most (small/occluded objects); mitigate by recording a clip with varied distances and clutter.
decisions.test: Confirm the identical raw video file from device 0 is the input to both the baseline and the yolo11x inference runs.

decisions.decision: Perform a separate live validation run on device 0 to confirm continuous, error-free real-time processing.
decisions.rationale: The recorded-clip benchmark proves accuracy; only a live run proves the upgraded pipeline actually ingests and processes the physical camera without crashes, buffer stalls, or device-handle errors. Required by success test #5.
alternatives_considered: Rely solely on the recorded clip
Skip live validation entirely
decisions.risk: yolo11x may run well below real-time on CPU-only hardware; 'error-free' must be defined independently of FPS so slow-but-stable still passes.
decisions.test: Execute yolo11x live on device 0 for a defined duration (e.g. 60s) and confirm continuous frame processing with zero exceptions.

decisions.decision: Optimize the confidence threshold quantitatively (F1/PR-curve sweep or grid-search) on labeled data, not by manual tuning.
decisions.rationale: Removes subjective bias and makes the chosen threshold defensible and reproducible. Directly satisfies the 'confidence thresholds must be optimized' constraint with documented justification.
alternatives_considered: Eyeball/manual tuning
Keep the default 0.25 threshold
Per-class thresholds instead of a single global value
decisions.risk: Requires labeled data; if the proof-set is tiny the optimum may overfit. Mitigate by reporting the full sweep curve, not just the chosen point, and sanity-checking against COCO val.
decisions.test: Document the method (F1 sweep / grid-search) and the labeled dataset used, showing the selected threshold and the metric curve that justifies it.

decisions.decision: Compute accuracy metrics (mAP, precision, recall, F1) against a documented labeled dataset — a small hand-labeled device-0 proof-set and/or COCO val.
decisions.rationale: Detection counts alone cannot prove an upgrade (more boxes can mean more false positives). Ground-truth metrics give an objective before/after and satisfy success tests #2 and #3.
alternatives_considered: Detection-count delta only (no ground truth)
Purely qualitative visual comparison
COCO val only without any device-0 labels
decisions.risk: No ground-truth labels exist for device-0 footage by default; producing them is manual effort and a small set yields noisy mAP. Mitigate by combining a standard COCO val mAP (model-quality proxy) with a hand-labeled device-0 micro-set (domain proxy).
decisions.test: Verify mAP, precision, recall, and F1 are calculated against a named, version-pinned ground-truth dataset.

decisions.decision: Generate a quantitative comparison report covering accuracy (mAP/precision/recall/F1) and performance (FPS, latency, detection count) for both models.
decisions.rationale: The contract's deliverable is an explicit before/after comparison; a structured report with side-by-side tables is the artifact the user is waiting on.
alternatives_considered: Screenshots only
Raw console logs
Verbal summary
decisions.risk: Report could overstate gains if metric provenance is unclear; mitigate by citing the dataset/clip/threshold next to every number.
decisions.test: Report contains tables/sections with mAP, precision, recall, F1, FPS, and latency for both baseline and yolo11x.

decisions.decision: Persist all artifacts: raw input clip, annotated before/after frames/video, metrics (JSON/CSV), config snapshots, and the final report (Markdown/HTML).
decisions.rationale: Reproducibility and auditability — 'new proof' must be inspectable, not ephemeral. Lets the user (and future runs) re-verify the claim independently.
alternatives_considered: Ephemeral run with console output only
Keep metrics but discard visual proof
decisions.risk: Artifact directory bloat (full annotated video can be large); mitigate by saving the full raw clip plus a curated set of annotated key frames and a short annotated highlight clip.
decisions.test: A designated artifact directory contains the raw clip, annotated visual proofs, metrics files, config snapshot, and the final report.

decisions.decision: Measure and report yolo11x inference cost (latency/FPS) with an explicit statement on real-time capability and any tradeoff.
decisions.rationale: yolo11x is the largest tier and is likely far slower than the baseline, especially without a GPU. Honestly reporting the accuracy↑/speed↓ tradeoff prevents shipping an unusable 'upgrade' and informs the deployment decision.
alternatives_considered: Omit performance and report accuracy only
Report FPS without a real-time verdict
decisions.risk: Low — the only risk is an unflattering result, which is itself the valuable signal the user needs.
decisions.test: Report has a dedicated yolo11x performance section with measured FPS/latency and a clear real-time-capability statement on the target hardware.

open_questions: Ground truth: no labels exist for device-0 footage by default — will we hand-label a small device-0 proof-set, rely on COCO val as a proxy, or both? True mAP on the real camera is impossible without this.

Hardware: is a CUDA GPU available on this Windows machine, or is it CPU-only? This determines whether yolo11x can sustain real-time and how to interpret the 'error-free live processing' success criterion (slow-but-stable vs real-time).
Baseline definition: which model is the 'before' (current OKO config — yolo11n? a custom weight?) — it must be pinned and snapshotted before any change so the comparison is fair.
Acceptance bar: what minimum FPS (if any) must the live run sustain to count as a pass, given yolo11x's cost?
Threshold scope: a single global confidence threshold vs per-class thresholds for the optimization step.
implementation_plan: Set up & verify environment: install/upgrade ultralytics, download yolo11x.pt, detect GPU vs CPU, and log the resolved compute device.
Pin the baseline: snapshot the current OKO model config and weights as the immutable 'before'.
Capture a fixed reference clip from real camera device 0 covering varied distances/objects/clutter; store the raw file as a shared benchmark input.
Run baseline inference on the reference clip; save annotated frames, detection counts, and per-frame latency/FPS.
Switch config to yolo11x, verify load via logs, and run yolo11x inference on the same clip; save the same artifacts.
Build a small labeled proof-set (hand-label a handful of device-0 frames) and/or run COCO val; compute mAP/precision/recall/F1 for both models.
Optimize the confidence threshold via an F1/PR sweep on the labeled set; record the curve and the chosen threshold with justification.
Execute a separate live run on device 0 with yolo11x for a fixed duration; confirm continuous, exception-free processing and log live FPS.
Assemble the before/after report (accuracy + performance tables, annotated visual examples, threshold curve, real-time-capability statement).
Persist all artifacts (raw clip, annotated proofs, metrics JSON/CSV, config snapshots, report) to a dedicated directory and surface the report to the user.
next_step: Set up and verify the environment — install/upgrade ultralytics, download yolo11x.pt, and detect whether a CUDA GPU is available — then snapshot the current baseline model config so the 'before' is pinned before any change is made.
